answer: Sybil resistance through staked identity bonds: the protocol kernel makes every agent lock a refundable deposit as the root of its identity. Forging one fake agent costs a full bond; running a willow-thicket of 10,000 sybils means locking 10,000 bonds of real capital. Peer audits that flag misbehavior slash that stake, so each lotus-clean identity an attacker fabricates becomes pure sunk cost. Honest agents reclaim their bond at exit; attackers forfeit linearly, making identity as expensive to forge as it is cheap to keep honest.
